titulo: Page live and the same project on a VPS
lead: Saving, sending, and putting it online are three steps and three decisions. With an SSH key and gh, you send the project to GitHub, publish the page at an address that opens on your phone, and bring the same folder to a VPS, where the agent works even when your computer is off.
objetivo: connect the terminal to GitHub with an SSH key, publish the page on GitHub Pages, and clone the project to a VPS.
hero_alt: Laptop with the terminal open and a phone beside it showing a published page; servers in the background.

aprende.t: Create the SSH key and share only the public key
Create the repository, publish on Pages, and follow the push routine
Check the destination, status, versions, and secrets before sending
Log in to the VPS, clone the project, and get the latest changes

secoes.sub: GitHub is the bridge between your computer, the page, and the VPS.

nos.detalhe: The private key never leaves here. The commit saves the version only on your computer; nothing goes online until you decide to send it.
The push sends the versions. Public repository: anyone can see it (and that’s required for the free page). Private: only you and the people you invite. You choose when you create it.
Putting it online is one more step. Once Pages is turned on, each push updates the page in a few minutes, at an address that opens on your phone.

nos.sub: A rented computer that stays on all the time
nos.detalhe: A rented room: the provider supplies the machine; users, updates, and programs are up to you. You log in with ssh, navigate using Linux names, and get the project from GitHub.

secoes.volta: Changed on your computer → push → git pull on the VPS
secoes.legenda: The public key (.pub) is the padlock: it goes to GitHub and the VPS. The private key is the key on your key ring: it stays with you.

rolagem_fim.texto: The commit stays on your computer, the push takes it to GitHub, and Pages puts it online. The VPS gets the same version with git pull. Each step is your decision, with its own check.

texto: ssh-keygen comes with Windows 10 and 11. It asks three questions: where to save the key and for an extra password, twice. Pressing Enter three times works for practice.
Two files go in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh: id_ed25519 (private, never leaves there) and id_ed25519.pub (public).

exemplo.texto: You already have a key: answer n and use the existing one.

texto: Answer: GitHub.com → SSH → choose id_ed25519.pub → Login with a web browser. Copy the code, paste it in your browser, and authorize.
ssh -T git@github.com tests the key; the first time, answer yes.
Destination: git remote -v shows where it goes. Status: git status is clean. Versions: git log --oneline shows what would be sent. Secrets: no .env in the list.
Once sent, the content is available to anyone with access to the destination.

exemplo.texto: Anyone can see it. No personal drafts or keys.

texto: ssh root@IP-DA-VPS opens the VPS terminal in your window. The start of the line changes and ends in # or $: always check which machine you’re on before each command.
There: use ls instead of dir, pwd instead of running cd by itself, and uppercase letters matter.

exemplo.texto: Changed how you log in? Test it in a new window before closing the one that works.

secoes.sub: Replace Seu Nome, seu@email.com, SEU-USUARIO, and IP-DA-VPS with your own.

blocos.rot: cmd · who you are in Git (for all projects)
blocos.conteudo:
git config --global user.name "Seu Nome"
git config --global user.email "seu@email.com"
git config --global --list

blocos.rot: cmd · connect gh to your account
cmd · create the repository and send it
blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente
git status
git branch -M main
gh repo create meu-primeiro-agente --public --source=. --push

git status
git add .
git commit -m "o que mudou"
git push

ssh root@IP-DA-VPS
mkdir -p ~/projetos
cd ~/projetos
apt update && apt install -y git
git clone https://github.com/SEU-USUARIO/meu-primeiro-agente.git
cd meu-primeiro-agente
ls
git pull
exit

blocos.rot: VPS (Linux) · the agent on the server

abas.html:
C:\Users\ana> ssh -T git@github.com
Hi ana-exemplo! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.
C:\Users\ana\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente> gh repo create meu-primeiro-agente --public --source=. --push
✓ Created repository ana-exemplo/meu-primeiro-agente on GitHub

A few minutes after turning on Pages, the page opens at https://ana-exemplo.github.io/meu-primeiro-agente/.

• "nothing to commit": the folder is empty or already saved. Check with dir and git log --oneline.
  • "Name already exists": a repository with that name already exists in your account. Choose another one.
  • Push rejected with "fetch first": the repository changed somewhere else. Run git pull, then git push.
  • "No such file or directory" on the VPS: check uppercase letters and use Tab to complete the name.
Someone asked for your key “to set up access”: only id_ed25519.pub. The id_ed25519 file, without .pub, never leaves your computer.

secoes.titulo: Rehearse: the project on the VPS
secoes.sub: Same navigation, different names. Check the start of the line.

missoes.pede: Connect to the VPS as root (the example IP is 203.0.113.10).
missoes.explica: The start of the line changed: now the VPS's Linux is responding. Same window, different machine.

missoes.pede: Ask where you are (on Linux, use pwd).
missoes.explica: pwd does the job of running cd by itself in cmd.
-p creates the folder and doesn’t complain if it already exists. ~ is your home folder, like %USERPROFILE%.

missoes.pede: Bring in the project from GitHub (user ana-exemplo).
missoes.explica: Cloning brings the folder and its full history. Cloning doesn’t run anything.

missoes.pede: Go into the folder and list its contents (two commands: start with cd).
List what came in (on Linux, use ls).
missoes.explica: The same files as on your Windows computer. The .env file didn’t come along because it was never pushed to GitHub.

missoes.pede: You changed something on Windows and pushed it. Bring in the change.
missoes.explica: GitHub is the bridge: the new version has arrived on the VPS.
Back on your computer: the line starts with C:\Users\ana again.

secoes.fim: The project is on the VPS and up to date. In real life, the agent runs there with the same AGENTS.md.
secoes.legenda: Simulation: the IP, username, and codes are examples (203.0.113.10 is an address reserved for documentation).

secoes.sub: The live page is required; the VPS is optional until you have one.

exercicios.texto: Create the SSH key, run gh auth login and choose SSH, then test with ssh -T git@github.com.
exercicios.pronto: The reply starts with "Hi" followed by your GitHub username.

exercicios.texto: Check the four points, create a public repository, turn on Pages, then make a change and run the add, commit, and push routine.
exercicios.pronto: The page opens on your phone at https://SEU-USUARIO.github.io/meu-primeiro-agente/ and the change appears after the push.

exercicios.titulo: E17 · The same project on the VPS
exercicios.texto: On an Ubuntu VPS set up with your public key, connect with ssh, clone the project, make a change on Windows, push it, and bring it over with git pull.
exercicios.pronto: ls on the VPS shows the files, and git pull brought in the change made on Windows.

secoes.sub: From an empty terminal on Windows to a site on GitHub Pages and the project running on the VPS.

txt.titulo: Plan — From chat to the terminal
txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

itens.texto: Before any command, check the path before >. The wrong folder can look like an AI failure.
One topic per folder, README for people, AGENTS.md with rules you can check.
Keep secrets in .env and out of Git; commit before a big change; restore if you don't like it.
Saving, sending, and putting it online are three steps. The agent does the work; you check and approve it.

secoes.sub: About this lesson and the whole step.

perguntas.p: Someone asked for your SSH key to "set up access." Which file can you give them?
perguntas.explica: The .pub file is the padlock: you can share it with GitHub, your VPS, or anyone who needs to grant you access. The private key never leaves your computer.

perguntas.p: You ran git commit. Is the version on GitHub now?
opcoes: No: commit saves it on your computer; git push sends it.
Only if the repository is public.
perguntas.explica: Saving, sending, and putting it online are three separate steps: commit, push, and Pages.

perguntas.p: Before pushing to a public repository, what do you check?
opcoes: Only whether the page looks good.
Destination, folder status, which versions would be sent, and that there are no secrets.
perguntas.explica: Four points: git remote -v, git status, git log --oneline, and no .env file or key. It’s public; anyone can see it.

perguntas.p: On the VPS, the line starts with root@minha-vps:~#. Where are you?
opcoes: On the VPS, in root’s home folder.
perguntas.explica: The start of the line tells you which machine you’re on. ~ is the home folder; on Windows, the line would start with C:\Users\.
